title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
problem: Autoregressive LLM serving suffers from high latency and computational overhead due to sequential token generation, where the full LLM must process tokens one at a time. This sequential nature creates a fundamental bottleneck in inference throughput.
motivation: Reducing LLM inference latency and computational cost is critical for real-world deployment of generative models in interactive applications.
method: SpecInfer leverages small speculative models to predict multiple candidate token sequences organized as a token tree. A novel tree-based parallel decoding mechanism verifies all candidate sequences simultaneously using the main LLM as a verifier rather than an incremental decoder, reducing end-to-end latency and computational requirements.
key_novelty: Tree-based parallel verification mechanism where the main LLM simultaneously verifies multiple candidate token sequences from speculative predictions rather than decoding incrementally.
contributions: Tree-based speculative inference framework for LLM serving
Novel tree-based parallel decoding and verification mechanism
Achieves 1.5-2.8× speedup for distributed inference and 2.6-3.5× for offloading-based inference
Provably preserves model quality while reducing latency and computation
